inspiration.observed_pattern: The source aggregates rows into JSON_ARRAYAGG(JSON_OBJECT(...)) and separately expands a JSON array parameter with JSON_TABLE into relational membership rows.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a batch-label normalization report. JSON_TABLE expands each stored label array with ordinality, and a grouped JSON_ARRAYAGG(JSON_OBJECT(...)) rebuilds an ordered array of positional label objects per batch. The source application schema, parameters, identifiers, and values are not copied.

fixture_notes: Batch 401 stores labels in the order amber, cobalt, ivory, while batch 402 stores mint and slate. JSON_TABLE ordinality must preserve each source position, and JSON_ARRAYAGG must rebuild the same order as labeled objects.
determinism_notes: Batch IDs, JSON arrays, ordinality, label values, object fields, aggregate ordering, and final batch ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE label_batches (batch_id INT PRIMARY KEY, batch_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, labels_json JSON NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO label_batches VALUES (401, 'warm palette', '["amber", "cobalt", "ivory"]'), (402, 'cool palette', '["mint", "slate"]')

steps.sql: WITH expanded_labels AS (SELECT b.batch_id, b.batch_name, jt.position, jt.label FROM label_batches AS b INNER JOIN JSON_TABLE(b.labels_json, '$[*]' COLUMNS (position FOR ORDINALITY, label VARCHAR(32) PATH '$')) AS jt ON TRUE) SELECT batch_id, batch_name, JSON_ARRAYAGG(JSON_OBJECT('position', position, 'label', label) ORDER BY position) AS normalized_labels FROM expanded_labels GROUP BY batch_id, batch_name ORDER BY batch_id

WITH expanded_labels AS (SELECT b.batch_id, b.batch_name, jt.position, jt.label FROM label_batches AS b INNER JOIN JSON_TABLE(b.labels_json, '$[*]' COLUMNS (position FOR ORDINALITY, label VARCHAR(32) PATH '$')) AS jt ON TRUE) SELECT batch_id, JSON_ARRAYAGG(JSON_OBJECT('label', label) ORDER BY position) AS labels_only FROM expanded_labels GROUP BY batch_id ORDER BY batch_id
